title: Understanding the Music Streaming Sessions mini dataset

scope.population: All rows in the two supplied mini CSV files
scope.purpose: Descriptive data understanding only; no models or test metrics
scope.split_status: No train/test split is created or used by this script
scope.caveat: This full-data exploration is disclosed. Do not describe a later test set as completely unseen during all exploration. Freeze a split before model selection and perform model-directed analysis on development data only.

sources.title: Mini-data archive named in the project
sources.role: Alternative archive reference; no hash or archive verification is performed by this script

access_limits: The official challenge page carries a July 2024 notice that original downloads are no longer available and directs requests to Spotify Research.

This analysis uses the user-supplied local CSVs. Public availability of an archive does not establish permission to redistribute its data; applicable terms must be checked before raw or record-level publication.
The local sample contains sessions of 10–20 tracks and a narrow popularity range. Findings should not be generalized to all streaming sessions or the full music catalog.
The supplied mini files contain no song titles, cross-session user IDs, uniform_random indicator or playlist snapshots. Shuffle alone cannot establish random treatment assignment.

size.note: Date endpoints do not imply coverage of every intervening day.

tables.row_unit: One track play within a session

important_variables.name: session_id
important_variables.meaning: Anonymous session key, not a user ID
important_variables.relevance: Split and group by session; not a predictor.

important_variables.name: session_position
important_variables.meaning: Track position within the recorded session
important_variables.relevance: Orders the observed and target windows.

important_variables.name: session_length
important_variables.meaning: Number of recorded tracks, capped at 20
important_variables.relevance: Supplied offline task information; eventual live length may be unknown.

important_variables.name: track_id_clean
important_variables.relevance: Join to track_features.track_id; not a song title.

important_variables.name: skip_2
important_variables.relevance: Prediction target; only first-half values may be model inputs. Exact time thresholds are not encoded in these CSV files.

important_variables.name: skip_1 / skip_3
important_variables.relevance: Different definitions; neither is interchangeable with skip_2.

important_variables.name: hist_user_behavior_reason_start
important_variables.relevance: Descriptive association only for future rows; model may use observed history.

important_variables.name: hist_user_behavior_reason_end
important_variables.relevance: Reveals outcome information; exclude future values.

important_variables.name: context_type / context_switch
important_variables.meaning: Playback source and whether context changed
important_variables.relevance: Context can change; use only first-half information for prediction.

important_variables.name: pause flags / seek counts
important_variables.meaning: Pauses before playback and seeks within a play
important_variables.relevance: Interaction fields, not safe future predictors despite hist_ names.

important_variables.name: premium / hist_user_behavior_is_shuffle
important_variables.relevance: Use observed values; shuffle does not imply uniform random ordering.

important_variables.name: date / hour_of_day
important_variables.relevance: Describe sample coverage; no cross-session user linkage.

important_variables.name: us_popularity_estimate
important_variables.relevance: Static reference signal; not assumed to be current Spotify API popularity.

important_variables.name: danceability / energy / valence / acousticness / speechiness
important_variables.relevance: Candidate features and explanatory profile charts.

important_variables.name: tempo / loudness
important_variables.relevance: Conventional units are BPM and dB; zero/extreme values are not automatically missing.

important_variables.name: acoustic_vector_0 ... acoustic_vector_7
important_variables.meaning: Eight supplied signed acoustic embedding components

issues.title: Some history profiles are empty
issues.detail: No first-half track has skip_2=false. Similarity features need an explicit fallback and missing-profile indicator.

issues.title: Non-skip_2 is not complete playback
issues.detail: These rows have both skip_2=false and not_skipped=false. Do not use the terms interchangeably.

issues.title: Many tracks have one observed play
issues.detail: Track-level skip rates based on very few plays are unstable; display denominators and label filtered views.

issues.title: Context can change inside a session
issues.detail: Use only observed first-half context when predicting the future.

issues.title: Premium status is not always constant
issues.detail: Retain these rows; use the final observed first-half value rather than a future value.

issues.title: Zero tempo values occur
issues.detail: Keep the original values. Zero may reflect an unestimated descriptor, but these files do not establish that interpretation.

issues.title: Zero time signatures occur
issues.detail: Do not automatically treat zero as a conventional musical meter or replace it without a documented rule.

issues.title: Not every acoustic feature is a probability
issues.detail: Signed vectors, positive loudness and flatness above one should not be clipped to [0,1].

data_quality.action: No cleaning, imputation, feature fitting or raw-file edits performed.

charts.title: Session lengths
charts.caption: Each session is counted once. The maximum recorded session length in these files is 20.
charts.insight: 5,066 of 10,000 sessions (50.7%) are at the 20-track maximum.
charts.alt: Bar chart of session counts for lengths 10 through 20, with the 20-track maximum highlighted.

charts.title: Skip rate by length and position
charts.caption: Track-play-weighted skip_2 rates. Denominators vary by position; later positions only include longer sessions.
charts.insight: Differences are descriptive associations, not evidence that session length or position causes skipping.
charts.alt: Two line charts of skip_2 rate by recorded session length and track position, with fixed 0–100% axes.

charts.title: Playback-start reasons
charts.caption: Each bar uses track plays with that start reason. Small categories can have unstable rates. Future start reasons are not permitted model features.
charts.insight: Playback-start reason is useful for descriptive understanding; using a future row's reason would break the observation boundary.
charts.alt: Horizontal bars show skip_2 rates by start reason, with each category's play count in its label.

charts.title: Listening contexts
charts.caption: Counts and rates are over track plays, not unique users or sessions. One session can contain multiple contexts.
charts.insight: 2,493 sessions contain more than one context type; future context cannot be assumed constant.
charts.alt: Two horizontal bar charts compare play counts and skip_2 rates across listening contexts.

charts.title: Context switches
charts.caption: The source-context chart uses the previous track's context and excludes first positions. The position chart includes recorded first-position flags whose pre-session context is unavailable.
charts.insight: Current context is not necessarily the source of a switch. Source categories are explicitly shifted within each session.
charts.alt: Line chart of context-switch rates by position and bar chart by previous context.

charts.title: Per-track skip rates
charts.caption: Each track contributes one rate, independent of how often it was played. The filtered view requires at least five observed plays; it changes the population.
charts.insight: 31,823 tracks (62.8%) appear once. Their observed rates can only be 0% or 100%.
charts.alt: Histograms compare all tracks' observed skip rates with the subset having at least five plays.

charts.title: Acoustic-feature distributions
charts.caption: Each metadata track is counted once. These are feature distributions, not feature importance or causal effects.
charts.insight: Features have different scales and shapes. Later preprocessing should consider these differences without using test outcomes.
charts.alt: Eight histograms show acousticness, danceability, energy, instrumentalness, speechiness, valence, tempo, and loudness over unique tracks.

charts.title: Popularity and track coverage
charts.caption: Both panels count unique tracks. Popularity is the supplied estimate; play counts refer only to this mini log.
charts.insight: Popularity ranges from 90.02 to 100.00; the sample does not span an unrestricted music catalog.
charts.alt: Histogram of the supplied popularity estimate and bars of track coverage by observed play-count bucket.

key_findings.title: Recorded sessions concentrate at the cap
key_findings.text: 5,066 of 10,000 sessions (50.7%) are at the 20-track maximum.

key_findings.title: Track rates need denominators
key_findings.text: 31,823 tracks (62.8%) appear once. Their observed rates can only be 0% or 100%.

key_findings.title: Popularity covers a narrow range
key_findings.text: Popularity ranges from 90.02 to 100.00; the sample does not span an unrestricted music catalog.

key_findings.title: Empty profiles need explicit handling
key_findings.text: 739 sessions have no non-skip_2 track in the first half.
